# **Treemap Visualisation with R**

The exercise has three parts. First, we will use functions from the `dplyr` package to prepare transaction data for a treemap. Then, we will create a static treemap using the `treemap` package. Finally, we will build an interactive treemap using the `d3treeR` package.

## **1. Installing and Launching R Packages**


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
pacman::p_load(treemap, treemapify, tidyverse) 
```
:::


## **2. Data Wrangling**

### **Importing the data set**

This chapter we will use realis2018.csv


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
realis2018 <- read_csv("data/realis2018.csv")
```
:::


### **Data Wrangling and Manipulation**

The data.frame `realis2018` contains detailed transaction records and is not suitable for treemap visualization. We will first prepare the data by grouping it by Project Name, Planning Region, Planning Area, Property Type, and Type of Sale.

Then, we will use summary statistics to calculate Total Units Sold, Total Area, Median Unit Price, and Median Transacted Price.

We will use `group_by()` and `summarise()` from the `dplyr` package. `group_by()` groups the data, and `summarise()` calculates values for each group to create a clean dataset for treemap plotting.

### **Grouped summaries without the Pipe**

The code chank below shows a typical two lines code approach to perform the steps.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
realis2018_grouped <- group_by(realis2018, `Project Name`,
                               `Planning Region`, `Planning Area`, 
                               `Property Type`, `Type of Sale`)
realis2018_summarised <- summarise(realis2018_grouped, 
                          `Total Unit Sold` = sum(`No. of Units`, na.rm = TRUE),
                          `Total Area` = sum(`Area (sqm)`, na.rm = TRUE),
                          `Median Unit Price ($ psm)` = median(`Unit Price ($ psm)`, na.rm = TRUE), 
                          `Median Transacted Price` = median(`Transacted Price ($)`, na.rm = TRUE))
```
:::


### **Grouped summaries with the *pipe***


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
realis2018_summarised <- realis2018 %>% 
  group_by(`Project Name`,`Planning Region`, 
           `Planning Area`, `Property Type`, 
           `Type of Sale`) %>%
  summarise(`Total Unit Sold` = sum(`No. of Units`, na.rm = TRUE), 
            `Total Area` = sum(`Area (sqm)`, na.rm = TRUE),
            `Median Unit Price ($ psm)` = median(`Unit Price ($ psm)`, na.rm = TRUE),
            `Median Transacted Price` = median(`Transacted Price ($)`, na.rm = TRUE))
```
:::


## **3. Designing Treemap with treemap Package**

**treemap** package is a R package specially designed to offer great flexibility in drawing treemaps. The core function, namely: *treemap()* offers at least 43 arguments. In this section, we will only explore the major arguments for designing elegent and yet truthful treemaps.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
realis2018_selected <- realis2018_summarised %>%
  filter(`Property Type` == "Condominium", `Type of Sale` == "Resale")
```
:::


### **Using the basic arguments**


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
treemap(realis2018_selected,
        index=c("Planning Region", "Planning Area", "Project Name"),
        vSize="Total Unit Sold",
        vColor="Median Unit Price ($ psm)",
        title="Resale Condominium by Planning Region and Area, 2017",
        title.legend = "Median Unit Price (S$ per sq. m)"
        )
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](Hands-on_Ex05E_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-6-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::

## **4. Designing Treemap using treemapify Package**


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot(data=realis2018_selected, 
       aes(area = `Total Unit Sold`,
           fill = `Median Unit Price ($ psm)`),
       layout = "scol",
       start = "bottomleft") + 
  geom_treemap() +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "light blue", high = "blue")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](Hands-on_Ex05E_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-13-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::


### **Defining hierarchy**


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot(data=realis2018_selected, 
       aes(area = `Total Unit Sold`,
           fill = `Median Unit Price ($ psm)`,
           subgroup = `Planning Region`),
       start = "topleft") + 
  geom_treemap()
```

![](Hands-on_Ex05E_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-14-1.png){width=672}
